objectives: Describe the legal requirements for the premises, the sign and the working hours of an office.
Name the seven registers and books of a notary and how long each one is kept.
Open, fill and close a notarial case file correctly.
Prepare documents in the format that Ordinance No. 32 requires.
List what the office must enter at once in the information system of the Notary Chamber.

cards.front: Minimum premises of a notary office?
cards.back: **Two or more functionally connected rooms** with the chancery and the official archive ([[znnd:13:2]]; [[n32:25]]).

cards.front: A clerk keeps the general register in a spreadsheet and prints nothing. What is wrong?
cards.back: A register kept on a computer is **printed**: each sheet dated, signed and sealed by the notary and joined to the previous one ([[n32:5:4|Art. 5(4)]]–[[n32:5:5|(5) Наредба № 32]]).

cards.front: The registry office receives documents until 16:00. When does work on deeds for entry stop?
cards.back: At **14:00**: at least two hours before the end of the reception time of the registry office ([[n32:27:2]]).

cards.front: How long can an office close temporarily?
cards.back: Up to **25 working days a year** and up to **2 hours a day** ([[n32:28]]).

cards.front: Name the seven registers and books of a notary.
cards.back: General register; alphabetical index; register of holographic wills and deposits; book of acts subject to entry; book of notarial wills; book of invitations, protests, protocols and copies; expense book ([[znnd:28а]]).

cards.front: The registration judge refused to enter a deed, and the regional court confirmed the refusal. Where does the deed go?
cards.back: Into the book of acts subject to entry, **with the court decision attached** ([[n32:6:2]]).

cards.front: How is the day closed in the registers?
cards.back: With the **signature and seal** of the notary before the first entry of the next day ([[n32:5:1]]).

cards.front: How is an error in a register corrected?
cards.back: By a **note** signed and sealed by the notary that says exactly how the correction reads; no erasures ([[n32:5:3]]).

cards.front: How many documents does a volume of a notarial book hold?
What goes into a notarial case file for a deed?
cards.back: The request, a copy of the signed deed, the declarations about the special requirements of the law, the proof of representation, and the accounting documents for the fees ([[n32:11]]).

cards.front: How long are case files for deeds kept?
cards.back: **5 years**; files for wills and deposits and decisions in circumstantial verifications: **100 years** ([[n32:10:5]]).

cards.front: The rubber seal of the notary is lost. What follows?
cards.back: The notary informs the Notary Chamber **at once**, and a new seal is made ([[n32:16]]). The seal is round, 40 mm, of the approved model ([[n32:14|Art. 14]]).

cards.front: How many copies of a draft deed that must be entered?
cards.back: At least **five** identical copies; wills: at least four ([[n32:18:1]]).

cards.front: How many copies go to the registry office?
cards.back: **Four** identical copies, one may be only signed, plus the request in two copies with the fee proof ([[n32:21:1]]).

cards.front: Deadline to send a notarial will to the registration judge?
Who may receive information from a notarial case file?
cards.back: Only the parties, their successors and their representatives; a non-lawyer needs an **express** power of attorney with a certified signature ([[znnd:28а:4]]).

quiz.question: The district court works from 9:00 to 17:00 and the registry office receives documents until 16:30. Until when may the office start work on deeds for entry?
options: Until 14:30
Until 16:30
Until 17:00
Until 15:30
quiz.explanation: [[n32:27:2|Art. 27(2) of Ordinance No. 32]]: work on deeds for entry ends at least two hours before the end of the reception time of the registry office: 16:30 minus two hours is 14:30. The deed must reach the registry office the same day ([[znnd:25:5]]).

quiz.question: A clerk made a mistake in the general register yesterday. How is it corrected?
options: With a note signed and sealed by the notary
With correction fluid and a new entry on the same line
By printing the page again without the wrong line
By a new line at the end of the register for that day
quiz.explanation: [[n32:5:2|Art. 5(2)]]–[[n32:5:3|(3) of Ordinance No. 32]]: no erasures, corrections or additions; an error is corrected by a note that says exactly how the correction reads, signed and sealed by the notary. Correction fluid or a reprinted page hides the history of the register.

quiz.question: How many general registers may a notary keep?
options: Only one
One per employee
One per type of act
As many as needed
quiz.explanation: [[n32:7:3|Art. 7(3) of Ordinance No. 32]]: a notary may not keep more than one general register; every act of the office goes into it in time order ([[n32:7:1|Art. 7(1)]]).

quiz.question: For which request is a notarial case file NOT opened?
options: A signature certification on a declaration
A notarial deed of sale of a garage in the district
A notarial will made in the office of the notary
A circumstantial verification of a village plot
quiz.explanation: [[n32:10:1|Art. 10(1) of Ordinance No. 32]]: a case file is opened for a notarial deed, for a will or a deposit, and for a circumstantial verification. A signature certification goes into the general register only ([[n32:7|Art. 7]]).

quiz.question: In 2026 the office sorts its archive. Which case file of 2019 may it destroy, after agreement with the State Archives?
options: The file of a sale deed
The file of a notarial will
The file of a deposited document
The decision in a circumstantial verification
quiz.explanation: [[n32:10:5|Art. 10(5) of Ordinance No. 32]]: files for deeds and circumstantial verifications are kept five years and then destroyed after agreement with the State Archives; files for wills and deposits, and the decisions in circumstantial verifications, are kept 100 years and go to the State Archives.

quiz.question: A testator revokes at your office a notarial will made by another notary. What does the office send, and to whom?
options: Copies to the registration judge and to the other notary, within 3 days
A copy to the registration judge only, within three days of the act of revocation
A copy to the other notary only, who holds the revoked will
Nothing; the revocation stays in the book of notarial wills
quiz.explanation: [[n32:21:2|Art. 21(2) of Ordinance No. 32]]: a notarial will or an act revoking a will goes to the registration judge in one copy within three days; when the revoked will is with another notary, that notary receives a copy within the same term, so that the will in the other office carries the note.

quiz.question: A sale deed is prepared. How many identical copies of the draft are needed as a minimum?
options: Five
Two
Three
Four
quiz.explanation: [[n32:18:1|Art. 18(1) of Ordinance No. 32]]: a deed subject to entry is prepared in at least five identical copies: one for the book, four for the registry office ([[n32:21:1|Art. 21(1)]]), and the parties get copies after the entry. A will needs at least four.

quiz.question: A testator deposits a holographic will. What must the notary do within three days?
options: Inform the registration judge of the testator's name
Open the envelope and announce the will to the family
Send a copy of the will to the heirs named in it
Publish a notice of the deposit in the State Gazette
quiz.explanation: [[n32:21:3|Art. 21(3) of Ordinance No. 32]]: within three days of the deposit the notary informs the registration judge in writing of the name of the testator. Nobody opens the envelope ([[zn:25:2]]), and the will is announced only after the death ([[zn:27]]).

quiz.question: Which power of attorney goes into the information system of the Chamber at once?
options: A power to manage a bank account, with a certified signature
A power to collect a child from school, with a certified signature
A power to receive a parcel at the post office, signed at home
A power to represent a tenant before the condominium
quiz.explanation: [[n32:9а::5|Art. 9а item 5 of Ordinance No. 32]]: extracts of powers for acts before banks, with a certified signature, are entered at once; items 1 and 7 to 10 add real estate, vehicles, the tax agency, investment firms and insurers. A power for a school, the post or the condominium is not in the list.

quiz.question: A neighbour asks for a copy of a deed in your archive "because he is curious". What do you do?
options: Refuse; only the parties, their successors and representatives
Give it against the fee for a copy, as to any client
Give it after the neighbour shows an identity card
Give only the first page, without the price and the names of the parties
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:28а:4]]: information from the case files is given only to the parties, their successors and their representatives by law or by a power; a non-lawyer needs an express power with a certified signature. Curiosity and a fee give no right.

quiz.question: What may the office sign NOT contain?
options: Commercial advertising
The working hours
The address
The district of the notary
quiz.explanation: [[n32:26:2|Art. 26(2)]]–[[n32:26:3|(3) of Ordinance No. 32]]: the sign may show the district, the address and the working hours, but may not be the subject of commercial advertising.

quiz.question: An office uses a computer to keep the general register. What must it do?
options: Print each sheet, dated, signed and sealed, and join it to the last
Keep the electronic file only, with a daily backup copy on a separate disk
Send the electronic file to the Notary Chamber every evening
Print the register once, at the end of the calendar year
quiz.explanation: [[n32:5:4|Art. 5(4)]]–[[n32:5:5|(5) of Ordinance No. 32]]: a register kept on a computer is printed; each sheet carries the date, the signature and the seal of the notary and is attached to the previous sheet, joined in at least two places. The paper register, not the file, is the register.
